bullets.title: NVDA +7% on blowout FY28 guide of ~70% YoY; $350B+ purchase commitments de-risk revenue
bullets.body: NVDA guided FY28 revenue growth of ~70% YoY (well above ~45% consensus), driven by agentic AI factory demand and supply-constrained backlog exceeding $2T. Total future commitments jumped to $366B (vs. $119B prior quarter), including $279B in supply/capacity and $36B in cloud agreements. AWS announced 2M additional GPUs (Blackwell Ultra, Rubin variants) for 2027-2028 deployment. Sell-side raised PTs broadly: JPM to $320, Bernstein to $400, Melius to $420, BofA Buy at $350, Citi $315, Goldman $300—though Goldman flagged elevated expectations may keep shares range-bound near-term.

bullets.title: NVDA acquires Hugging Face for ~$13B; controls open-source AI model distribution
bullets.body: NVDA is acquiring Hugging Face for approximately $12.9-13B (>85x trailing sales), gaining control over the largest open-source model repository and developer distribution layer. The move mirrors Microsoft's GitHub ownership model—supporting competitors while making NVDA's CUDA/silicon ecosystem more convenient. HF ownership also helps de-risk NVDA's $36B cloud backstop commitments by generating third-party demand.

bullets.title: Nasdaq vol (VXN) falls into 'investable bucket' post-NVDA; SPX +0.6%, NDX +1.0%
bullets.body: NVDA earnings pushed NazVol/VXN below 22, shifting the NASDAQ into the 'investable bucket' vol regime according to Hedgeye. SPX is up ~0.6% to 7,720 and NDX +1.0%. SPX is pricing an additional 35bps of movement ahead of Fed Chair Warsh's Jackson Hole speech tomorrow at 10am ET. S&P futures were +0.32% pre-open with the 10-year yield +1bp to 4.66%.

bullets.title: Semiconductor tariff expansion risk: White House weighing chips, laptops, servers
bullets.body: Per Politico, the Trump administration is considering a new round of sweeping semiconductor tariffs that would expand beyond current exemptions to include laptops and servers. MS TMT noted the move represents a shift away from data center exemptions and is a key near-term risk for the semis complex, particularly given NVDA's supply-constrained demand backdrop.

bullets.title: Jackson Hole: Warsh speech tomorrow is the binary for rates, dollar, and risk assets
bullets.body: Markets are pricing 35bps of additional SPX volatility ahead of Fed Chair Warsh's 10am ET speech Friday at Jackson Hole. 57% of dollar options flows this week favor further USD gains (up from 43% last week), reflecting bullish dollar hedges. A neutral-to-dovish signal from Warsh would shift focus to 8,000 SPX support into September OPEX. Fed's Schmid meanwhile stated inflation remains 'stubborn and sticky,' interest rates are not restraining the economy, and the midterms won't affect the October meeting decision.

bullets.title: ECB minutes lean hawkish: September hike 'likely done deal,' December risks skewed higher
bullets.body: ECB July minutes showed some members supported a July hike; credit growth accelerated to 4.4% 3m/3m saar and M3 rose €39B. Council member Radev pegged the neutral rate at 'probably 2.5%', above official staff estimates. September hike is described as a 'done deal' with risks skewed to a final hike in December. ECB records show labor markets have weakened, reducing second-round wage-price spiral risk, but energy price pass-through into consumer prices may not appear until August data.

bullets.title: Q2 U.S. corporate profits surged 22.8% YoY, highest since 4Q21; S&P EPS beat rate 94%
bullets.body: U.S. corporate profits grew 22.8% YoY in 2Q26 (vs. 12.8% prior quarter), the strongest growth since 4Q21's post-pandemic rebound of 27.9%. With 477 S&P 500 companies reported, EPS is tracking +52% YoY acceleration. One source cited 94% of S&P 500 Q2 reporters meeting or exceeding EPS estimates with actual growth of 46% vs. 21% forecast, and 51% of S&P 500 raised capex >10% YoY vs. a 41% long-run average.

bullets.title: July PCE data: supercore CPI cools, savings rate rises to 4-month high, capex strong
bullets.body: Supercore CPI and PCE both cooled in July, moving toward the Fed's 2% target. Personal savings rate bounced to 3.0% (4-month high, up 40bps from June's 2.6%). Core capital goods shipments rose +1.4% m/m in July, one of the strongest year-to-date reads. July PCE showed $86.2B services spending gain offset by $49.9B goods decline, continuing the shift from goods to services.

bullets.title: Initial claims 203k, near historic lows; labor market robust
bullets.body: Initial claims fell 4k w/w to 203k, with the 4-week average at 206k—both historically low and consistent with private payroll growth of 1.0-1.5% YoY. Continuing claims edged down 18k to 1,778k. The data reinforces a resilient labor market backdrop ahead of next week's NFP (Sept 4).

bullets.title: Kansas City Fed manufacturing rose to 10 in August; August ISM tracking 54.8
bullets.body: The Kansas City Fed manufacturing headline composite rose to 10 from 9 in August with strong production and strengthening new orders, though labor demand softened. Prices paid and received both accelerated, with prices received diverging from deceleration seen in other regional surveys. August ISM Manufacturing PMI is tracked at 54.8, down from July's 55.6.

bullets.title: Strait of Hormuz: Qatar-Iran discuss temporary shipping corridor; Kuwait/Qatar ramping oil flows
bullets.body: Qatar and Iran discussed a phased framework including a temporary shipping corridor and joint mine-clearing project in the Strait of Hormuz. Kuwait and Qatar are simultaneously ramping crude exports through the strait, helping keep oil prices in check. Iraq offered oil exports via alternative routes outside Hormuz for the first time since the war began. WTI is trading at ~$82. JPMorgan warns global food inflation could surge from 2.8% to 5% by early 2027 due to nitrogen fertilizer constraints from the Hormuz closure (fertilizer covers ~50% of global crops).

bullets.title: Fed's Schmid: energy shock leaking into economy; inflation 'stubborn and sticky'
bullets.body: Fed's Schmid flagged that the energy shock is transmitting into economy-wide inflation, with inflation described as 'stubborn and sticky.' He also noted current interest rates are not restraining the U.S. economy, does not view Fed credibility as damaged, and said the midterms won't affect the October meeting decision. Goolsbee separately indicated he is assessing whether inflation impacts will be lasting or transitory.

bullets.title: Treasury doubled buybacks to $4B; 30yr at 5.30% seen as intervention signal, not floor
bullets.body: Treasury doubled buybacks to approximately $4B (~14% of issuance) and will hold November coupon auctions flat or reduce them with a shift toward T-bills. 5.30% on the 30-year is viewed as the Treasury's intervention signal, not a structural floor, as underlying fiscal and inflation headwinds persist. The debasement trade is rotating from steepeners into gold and short dollar. Global growth is holding at ~2.6% despite the oil shock, with inflation up 0.75pp to 3.4% YoY.

bullets.title: Bank of Korea hikes 25bp to 3.0% for second consecutive time on AI-driven semiconductor boom
bullets.body: South Korea's BoK raised rates 25bp to 3.00%, citing AI-driven semiconductor exports lifting growth, inflation (core raised to 2.5%), and housing costs. GDP forecast was upgraded to 3.3% for 2026 (from 2.6%) and 2.9% for 2027. Tech/semiconductor exports to the U.S. remain elevated though real volumes have softened; exports ex-U.S. hit new records at 45% of GDP. Real GDP expected to cool from 3.7% in 2Q26 to 3.1% by 1Q27 from cumulative tightening.

bullets.title: AI infrastructure capex cycle broadening beyond hyperscalers: 45GW compute added, $500B private financing
bullets.body: Google and NVDA alone are expected to add ~45GW of compute capacity in the next year. A new $500B private capital financing platform anchored by Apollo, BlackRock, Blackstone, Brookfield, Goldman, and KKR is positioned as the balance sheet of the AI capex cycle, financing land, power, shells, and neocloud capacity. AI investment is now expanding from hyperscalers and chipmakers into data centers, networking, power, materials, and cybersecurity. The total AI buildout is estimated to require $7T in AI-related debt and $12T in total financing.

bullets.title: Jefferies semis conference: AI demand remains strong, supply is the binding constraint
bullets.body: Jefferies' semis conference highlighted that supply—not demand—is the bottleneck for AI compute. COHR reports 1.6T transceiver optics demand tracking 100M units in 2027 with a potential supply shortage for 12-18+ months. NVDA secured substrates and DRAM, providing a competitive advantage; AMD locked in substrate capacity during the pandemic. CPO adoption is delayed to 2H 2028, creating near-term openings for NPO proprietary architectures. Management teams at conference were uniformly positive, seeing market sentiment as overly pessimistic on AI frontier economics.

bullets.title: Consumer sentiment deteriorating: grocery affordability concerns jump from 24% to 41% since April
bullets.body: 41% of Americans are now concerned about affording groceries over the coming months, up sharply from 24% in April, signaling deteriorating consumer confidence on cost of living. Real disposable income has effectively flatlined for over a year, remaining well below pre-pandemic trend. Despite this, consumer spending is shifting from goods to services, with July PCE showing $86.2B services gains offsetting $49.9B goods declines.

bullets.title: Week ahead: NFP Sept 4, ISMs, AVGO earnings Sept 2, US-China AI talks and Xi visit Sept 24
bullets.body: JPM's macro week ahead flags NFP on Sept 4 at 8:30am ET, ISM-Mfg on Sept 1, ISM-Services on Sept 3, and the Fed Beige Book on Sept 2. AVGO reports earnings on Sept 2. US-China AI talks are planned for September with a potential Xi visit to the U.S. on Sept 24. The US-China trade truce expires Nov 1. Meta Connect is Sept 23-24, and AWS re:Invent runs Nov 30-Dec 4.

bullets.title: META $18B settlement removes social media addiction overhang; EU demands screen time controls
bullets.body: Meta reached a mid-trial settlement with 52 state attorneys general for up to $18B over 10 years on social media addiction claims, removing a key legal overhang. Separately, the EU Commission ordered Meta to improve screen time management and parental controls. Meta is also reported to be projecting up to $10B annually in spending on Anthropic's AI models for internal tools and its upcoming personal assistant product 'Hatch,' and is seeking to issue KRW 1T+ bonds in South Korea.

bullets.title: Dollar strength building into Warsh speech; AUD surges on RBA hike repricing to 40%
bullets.body: Currency traders increased bullish USD options flows to 57% of volume (from 43% last week) ahead of Warsh's Jackson Hole speech. On the other side, Australia's July CPI printed 3.5% YoY with trimmed mean at 3.6%, pushing September RBA hike odds from under 10% to ~40%. Goldman recommends buying AUDUSD 0.7250/0.7375 call spread at 23bps with spot at 0.7182.
